title: Top K Frequent Elements
statement: You get a list of integers and a number k. Return the k values that appear most often. The answer is guaranteed to be unique, and you may return the values in any order. Aim for better than sorting everything.

example.caption: 1 appears three times and 2 appears twice. They are the two most frequent values.

output.label: slots: the frequency is the index

idea.sentence: Count each value, then file it into a slot numbered by its count. Read the slots from the highest number down and stop after k values.

jargon.plain: How many times a value appears in the list.
Sorting by dropping items into numbered slots, so the slot number does the ordering. No comparisons needed.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: the list, then k, e.g. [1,1,1,2,2,3], 2

vars.meaning: number of integers in the list

rows.name: Count and sort
rows.note: Sort the distinct values by count. At most n distinct values.

rows.name: Count and min-heap of size k
rows.note: Keep only the k best so far. Good when k is small. Not traced here.

rows.name: Count and buckets
rows.note: A count is never more than n, so n+1 slots are enough. Filing is one step per value, walking the slots is at most n steps.

fast.takeaway: A count can only be between 1 and n. That makes the count itself a usable array index, so no sorting is needed.

stages.title: Count
stages.note: One pass builds a map from value to how many times it appears.

stages.title: File by count
stages.note: Make n+1 empty slots. Put each value into the slot numbered by its count.

stages.title: Read from the top
stages.note: Walk the slots from the highest count down. Take their values until you have k.

edges.title: One number
edges.why: One value, one slot. The first slot read gives the answer.

edges.title: All the same
edges.why: The only value lands in slot 4, the last one. Slots 1 to 3 stay empty.

edges.title: k is every value
edges.why: The walk goes all the way down to slot 1 before it has k values.

edges.title: Zero and negatives
edges.why: Values are map keys, never indexes. Only the counts are used as slot numbers.

gotchas.text: Array.from({ length: n + 1 }, () => []) makes separate inner arrays. new Array(n + 1).fill([]) makes one shared array in every slot, so every value lands everywhere.
out.push(...bucket) passes each item as an argument. A very large bucket can overflow the call stack. A plain for loop is safe.
If you sort the entries instead, remember Array.sort with no comparer orders as text. Counts 10 and 9 would sort as "10" < "9". Use (a, b) => b[1] - a[1].
Map iteration order is random. Values inside one slot can come out in any order, which is fine here because any order is allowed. Compare after sorting in tests.
make([][]int, n+1) gives nil inner slices. append works on a nil slice, so no setup is needed per slot.

recap.key: Count each value. The count is a slot number between 1 and n. Read slots from the top until k values are taken.
moves: Count each value in a map
Make n+1 slots and file each value by its count
Walk slots from n down to 1
Stop once you have k values
